question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party, state institutions, and the military through loyal appointees and ongoing anti-corruption campaigns that have neutralized potential rivals. Recent developments, including his active role in setting 2026 economic priorities, advancing the 15th Five-Year Plan, and engaging in high-level diplomacy, reinforce trader expectations that he will pursue a fourth term at the 2027 Party Congress rather than exit office. The absence of visible factional challenges or succession planning further supports the 95.5% implied probability on "No." Rare scenarios that could still shift outcomes include a sudden health event, elite discontent ahead of the congress, or an unforeseen domestic crisis severe enough to prompt resignation or removal.

eventMetadata.context_description: The fragmented Democratic field two years out from the 2028 primaries keeps the nomination market tightly contested, with trader consensus assigning the highest probabilities to Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff amid uncertainty over the party's post-2024 direction. Progressive momentum around economic populism and generational change has boosted Ocasio-Cortez's position, while Newsom draws support from his record of state-level opposition to Republican policies and fundraising connections. Ossoff has gained through visibility on affordability and institutional issues. The DNC's proposed early primary calendar starting in South Carolina adds another variable, as does the broader debate over whether to emphasize centrist or activist approaches. No major candidate has formally entered the race, leaving room for shifts based on midterm results, polling trends, or endorsements.
